definition: Interface Parity means that CLI and MCP operations representing the same domain intent enforce the same domain invariants, defaults, ordering, validation, error meaning, and result meaning. Adapter mechanics may differ only when classified explicitly.

current_parity_values.conformant: Current adapters have equivalent observable domain behavior.
current_parity_values.drift: Both adapters expose the intent, but observable behavior differs.
current_parity_values.not_comparable: The intent currently exists in one adapter or is absent from both.

target_status_values.conformant: The required target contract is implemented.
target_status_values.gap_cli: The CLI lacks required target behavior.
target_status_values.gap_both: Both adapters lack required target behavior.
target_status_values.intentional_cli_only: The intent is deliberately available only through the CLI.
target_status_values.intentional_mcp_only: The intent is deliberately available only through MCP.
target_status_values.legacy_cutover: The current surface is legacy and must be replaced by canonical intents rather than expanded.

adapter_mechanics: CLI text rendering, --json selection, prompts, confirmations, and partial-success batching are presentation or invocation mechanics.
MCP protocol envelopes, current context, per-call workspace_root, and loop-equivalent single-target calls are adapter mechanics.
Loop-equivalent MCP calls satisfy parity for CLI batches because current CLI batches are partial-success convenience, not atomic multi-Issue transactions.
Workspace initialization and permanent Issue deletion are intentionally CLI-only. MCP context inspection and selection are intentionally MCP-only.

target_rules.contract: List Issues, Ready Issues, and Stale Issues require an explicit limit in both adapters.
List Issues orders newest-created first; Ready Issues uses Hybrid ordering; Stale Issues orders oldest-updated first.
Stale Issues excludes Closed Issues unless the caller explicitly filters for Closed Workflow State.
Both adapters enforce the canonical prefix-suffix Issue ID grammar before lookup or mutation.
Labels are 1-50 lowercase ASCII alphanumeric characters with internal hyphens or underscores, start and end alphanumeric, and contain no consecutive separators.
Open, In Progress, and Closed are the only Workflow States; Blocked and Ready are derived conditions.
Assignment changes through Claim and Release intents, not blind general update. Closing clears Assignment and reopening produces an unassigned Open Issue.
Blocking Dependency, Parentage, Related Association, and Discovery Origin use dedicated intents and their ADR-0002 invariants; generic dependency operations are legacy.
Show Issue returns the Issue and complete canonical relationship views in both adapters; presentation and protocol envelopes may differ.
Shared intents return the same domain information and error meaning even when adapter envelopes differ.

operations.title: Initialize Workspace
operations.target: Create the Workspace's Rivets files and choose its Issue ID prefix.

arguments.prefix: optional string; absent prompts unless --quiet; default proj

cli.result: Creates .rivets/config.yaml, .rivets/issues.jsonl, and .rivets/.gitignore with the selected Issue ID prefix; quiet suppresses text output.

operations.risk: MCP clients cannot create repository files accidentally.
operations.required_resolution: Retain as an explicit CLI-only safety exception.

operations.title: Workspace Information
operations.target: Return Workspace root, storage location/backend, Issue ID prefix, and configuration identity without issue statistics.

cli.result: Database path, Issue ID prefix, and total/open/in_progress/legacy blocked/closed counts.

mcp.result: No shared Workspace Information tool; where_am_i is context inspection.

operations.risk: Neither adapter currently returns the required shared Workspace root, configured storage/backend, Issue ID prefix, and configuration identity contract.
operations.required_resolution: Separate information from statistics, source fields from actual Workspace configuration, and add the shared Workspace Information intent to MCP.
differences: CLI info hardcodes the default issues.jsonl path and mixes configuration identity with legacy Workflow State counts.
No shared MCP Workspace Information tool exists; where_am_i is MCP-only context inspection.

operations.title: Create Issue
operations.target: Atomically create a valid Issue with optional initial Note and validated initial canonical Issue Relationships.

arguments.title: optional at parse time; interactive when absent
arguments.kind: optional Issue Kind; current default Task
arguments.prerequisite: repeatable canonical Blocking prerequisite Issue ID

cli.result: Issue created atomically with every validated Blocking prerequisite.

arguments.title: required string
arguments.issue_kind: optional Issue Kind; current default Task

mcp.result: Issue; initial relationships are always empty.

differences: CLI atomically accepts repeated validated Blocking prerequisites; MCP Create accepts no initial relationships.
Neither adapter can express every canonical initial Parentage, Related Association, or Discovery Origin.
CLI may prompt for a missing title while MCP requires it; this is an intentional adapter mechanic.
MCP accepts a hidden migration-only issue_type alias that is absent from its public schema.
operations.risk: Equivalent canonical relationship-bearing creates cannot be expressed across adapters, and compatibility-only input remains at a public MCP seam.
operations.required_resolution: Give both adapters equivalent validated canonical initial-relationship inputs while preserving CLI prompting and MCP envelopes as adapter mechanics.

operations.title: List Issues
operations.target: Filter Issues by Workflow State, Priority, Issue Kind, Assignee, and Label; require an explicit limit; order newest-created first.

arguments.status: optional Workflow State; currently also accepts legacy Blocked and CLI-only in-progress alias
arguments.label: optional string

arguments.status: optional raw string; current canonical spellings plus legacy Blocked
arguments.label: optional string

differences: CLI defaults to Priority ordering and limit 50; MCP fixes newest-created ordering and defaults to 100.
Both accept legacy Blocked Workflow State; CLI alone accepts the in-progress alias.
CLI constrains Priority to P0-P4; MCP accepts any u8.
MCP accepts a hidden migration-only issue_type alias.
Newest-created ties are not deterministically ordered.
operations.risk: Equivalent omitted inputs return different subsets/order, validation differs, and implicit truncation can hide Issues.
operations.required_resolution: Require a positive explicit limit, use deterministic newest-created ordering in both adapters, enforce canonical Workflow State and Priority, and publish the same constrained schemas.

operations.title: Show Issue
operations.target: Return the Issue plus complete canonical relationship views.

arguments.issue_ids: one or more canonical Issue IDs

cli.result: Array of enriched Issue details with blocking_prerequisites and blocking_dependents; legacy dependencies omitted.

mcp.result: Bare Issue with no canonical relationship views.

differences: CLI returns enriched Issue details with Blocking prerequisites and dependents; MCP returns a bare Issue despite its handler description.
Neither adapter returns complete Parentage, Related Association, and Discovery Origin views.
CLI validates Issue ID grammar; MCP constructs IssueId from an unconstrained string.
CLI batch is loop-equivalent and intentional.
operations.risk: MCP clients cannot observe Blocking relationship context and neither adapter provides the complete canonical relationship view.
operations.required_resolution: Return complete canonical relationship views from both adapters and adopt shared canonical Issue ID parsing; retain adapter-specific batch/envelope mechanics.

operations.title: Update Issue
operations.target: Update mutable descriptive fields and Issue Kind; reject empty updates; Assignment, Labels, Notes, relationships, and lifecycle transitions use intent-named operations.
differences: CLI rejects empty updates; MCP accepts them and advances updated_at.
MCP replaces Labels while CLI requires dedicated add/remove for label mutation.
CLI appends Notes through update; MCP uses add_note.
Assignment clearing uses an explicit CLI flag versus an MCP empty-string sentinel.
Both expose legacy Workflow State and blind Assignment mutation through general Update.
CLI validates Issue ID and Priority grammar before mutation; MCP uses unconstrained strings and weaker numeric schema.
MCP accepts a hidden migration-only issue_type alias.
operations.risk: Adapter choice changes accepted fields, no-op mutation history, validation, and ownership/lifecycle semantics.
operations.required_resolution: Restrict general Update to canonical descriptive fields and Issue Kind, reject empty requests, adopt canonical Issue ID parsing, and route Assignment, Labels, Notes, relationships, and lifecycle through dedicated intents.

operations.title: Close Issue
operations.target: Close an Issue, append an optional reason Note, clear Assignment, and preserve canonical relationship invariants.
differences: CLI batch/confirmation behavior is an intentional adapter mechanic.
CLI validates Issue ID grammar before mutation; MCP uses an unconstrained string.
Both preserve Assignment instead of enforcing the canonical close/reopen Assignment transition.
operations.risk: Invalid Issue IDs fail differently and both adapters violate canonical Assignment/Workflow transition invariants.
operations.required_resolution: Implement canonical close once at the shared mutation seam, including Assignment semantics and canonical Issue ID parsing.

operations.title: Reopen Issue
operations.target: Reopen a Closed Issue as unassigned Open and append an optional reason Note.
differences: CLI batch/confirmation behavior is an intentional adapter mechanic.
CLI validates Issue ID grammar before mutation; MCP uses an unconstrained string.
Both preserve Assignment instead of enforcing the canonical close/reopen Assignment transition.
operations.risk: Invalid Issue IDs fail differently and both adapters violate canonical Assignment/Workflow transition invariants.
operations.required_resolution: Implement canonical reopen once at the shared mutation seam, including Assignment semantics and canonical Issue ID parsing.

operations.title: Delete Issue Permanently
operations.target: Permanently delete one Issue through an explicitly confirmed human-facing operation.

cli.result: Text 'Deleted issue: ID' or JSON {deleted: ID, status: success}; confirmation is bypassed only by --force/--yes.

operations.risk: Permanent deletion lacks a recovery path and MCP has no human confirmation channel.
operations.required_resolution: Retain as an explicit CLI-only safety exception.

operations.title: Ready Issues
operations.target: Return Open, unblocked Issues using assignee-aware canonical readiness, require limit, and use Hybrid ordering.
differences: CLI defaults to limit 10 and exposes Hybrid/Priority/Oldest; MCP defaults to 100 and fixes Hybrid.
CLI constrains Priority to P0-P4; MCP accepts any u8 and a hidden issue_type alias.
Shared storage excludes only Closed, so In Progress and legacy Blocked Issues can be returned as Ready.
Legacy ParentChild edges propagate blockedness, contrary to canonical Parentage.
operations.risk: Adapters truncate the frontier differently and current lifecycle/Parentage semantics can offer or hide the wrong work.
operations.required_resolution: Require a positive explicit limit, use shared deterministic Hybrid ordering, enforce Open/unblocked/Assignment-aware readiness, remove Parentage propagation, and align schemas.

operations.title: Add Associated Resource
operations.target: Add a validated Associated Resource with one target, role, and optional label.
differences: CLI validates Issue ID grammar before the operation; MCP uses an unconstrained string.
CLI publishes Resource Role as an enum and enforces exactly one URL/Path at parse time; MCP publishes a plain role string and optional URL/Path fields, then validates at runtime.
operations.risk: MCP public schema and Issue ID validation are weaker than CLI even where runtime Resource semantics match.
operations.required_resolution: Adopt canonical Issue ID parsing and publish canonical Resource constraints in MCP while preserving stable Resource identity and insertion order.

operations.title: Update Associated Resource
operations.target: Update supplied Resource fields while preserving stable identity and order.
differences: CLI validates Issue ID grammar before the operation; MCP uses an unconstrained string.
CLI schema requires at least one change and publishes exclusive target/label groups plus Resource Role enum; MCP schema makes fields independently optional and relies on runtime rejection.
operations.risk: MCP public schema and Issue ID validation are weaker than CLI even where runtime Resource semantics match.
operations.required_resolution: Adopt canonical Issue ID parsing and publish canonical Resource constraints in MCP while preserving stable Resource identity and insertion order.

operations.title: Remove Associated Resource
operations.target: Remove a Resource by stable ID while preserving remaining IDs and order.
differences: CLI validates Issue ID grammar before the operation; MCP uses an unconstrained string.
operations.risk: MCP public schema and Issue ID validation are weaker than CLI even where runtime Resource semantics match.
operations.required_resolution: Adopt canonical Issue ID parsing and publish canonical Resource constraints in MCP while preserving stable Resource identity and insertion order.

operations.title: List Associated Resources

operations.title: Stale Issues
operations.target: Return non-Closed Issues older than the requested age, require limit, and order oldest-updated first; Closed is included only when explicitly filtered.

cli.result: Issue list; Closed excluded when status omitted; oldest-updated first.

mcp.result: Issue list; Closed included when status omitted; storage newest-created order.

differences: CLI defaults to limit 50, excludes Closed when status is omitted, and orders oldest-updated; MCP defaults to 100, includes Closed, and inherits newest-created order.
Both accept legacy Blocked Workflow State; CLI alone accepts the in-progress alias.
Ordering ties are not deterministic.
operations.risk: Equivalent omitted inputs return different Issues and MCP can omit the stalest records while including Closed work.
operations.required_resolution: Require a positive explicit limit, exclude Closed by default, use deterministic oldest-updated ordering, and share canonical Workflow State validation.

operations.title: Blocked Issues
operations.target: Return Issues blocked by unresolved Blocking Dependencies with optional Assignee filtering and blocker details.

arguments.assignee: advertised optional string but currently ignored

differences: CLI advertises an ignored Assignee filter; MCP has no Assignee filter.
CLI JSON names blocker rows blocked_by while MCP names them blockers.
Issue and blocker ordering is not deterministic.
Legacy Blocked Workflow State can still appear; direct Blocking computation itself is already typed.
operations.risk: CLI silently ignores input, adapters cannot express equivalent filtered queries, and result order/shape is unstable.
operations.required_resolution: Implement equivalent Assignee filtering, canonical Workflow State handling, deterministic Issue/blocker ordering, and the same semantic blocker payload across adapters.

operations.title: Workspace Statistics
operations.target: Return total Issues, counts by canonical Workflow State and Priority, derived Ready count, and derived Blocked count.

cli.result: Statistics; currently mixes legacy Blocked status with blocked-by-dependency count.

mcp.result: No registered tool; unused StatsResponse exists.

operations.risk: MCP has no equivalent Workspace health view and CLI statistics do not satisfy canonical Workflow State/Ready/Blocked meaning.
operations.required_resolution: Add shared Workspace Statistics to MCP and align both adapters to canonical Workflow State, deterministic Priority counts, Ready, and Blocked definitions.
differences: CLI statistics publish legacy Blocked Workflow State and make Priority counts conditional on --detailed.
CLI Ready count uses legacy broad readiness and ParentChild propagation.
No MCP statistics tool is registered; StatsResponse is unused.

CLI omitted depth defaults to 5; MCP omitted depth means unlimited.
Explicit depth, direction, deterministic BFS rows, and result meaning otherwise match.
